label: Missing security response headers
description: Absence of CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and similar hardening headers.
falsifier_hint: All headers present with a defensible policy, or endpoint is non-browser/non-HTML.
minimum_proof: Raw response headers showing the missing header on a security-relevant route.
na_patterns: Header absent on a non-HTML/JSON API
CSP present but only report-only mode
overclaim_traps: Treating any missing header as a High without a demonstrated impact chain.

label: Information disclosure / secret leak
description: Leaked secrets, backup files, debug endpoints, or sensitive metadata.
falsifier_hint: The exposed value is public/publishable, expired, or the endpoint is intended to be public.
minimum_proof: Exact location plus one authenticated call proving the secret is live and privileged; secret redacted in report.
na_patterns: Public client-side keys (Maps browser key, Firebase apiKey, Stripe pk_, Sentry DSN)
Expired/revoked credentials
Placeholder/test values
overclaim_traps: Reporting presence of a secret as impact instead of what it unlocks.
Treating any long random string as a leaked secret.

label: Reflected XSS
description: Untrusted input reflected into the HTML response without encoding, executing as script in the victim origin.
falsifier_hint: Payload is HTML-encoded or stripped, or execution happens in a sandboxed/null origin.
minimum_proof: JS execution on target origin (alert(document.domain)); injection context and type stated.
na_patterns: alert(1) on null origin or sandboxed iframe
Self-XSS
HTML injection without JS execution
overclaim_traps: Session theft claim when cookie is HttpOnly.
Account takeover without a takeover PoC.
CSP bypass without showing CSP header + technique.

label: SQL injection
description: Untrusted input concatenated into SQL, allowing data extraction or time/boolean oracles.
falsifier_hint: WAF blocked the payload, or only a generic 500/error message without controlled injection.
minimum_proof: Data extraction (sentinel value/table/version), controlled SLEEP(n) with varying n, or controlled boolean oracle with response differential.
na_patterns: WAF blocked the payload then claimed SQLi
Error mentioning SQL without controlled injection
Generic HTTP 500 on quote characters
DB banner leaked without proving injection
overclaim_traps: Full database compromise without dumping a controlled sentinel row.
Escalating into destructive post-exploitation past proof.

label: Path traversal / LFI
description: Reading files outside the intended directory via ../ or absolute paths.
falsifier_hint: Payload normalized/blocked by framework or WAF, or only an error without file content.
minimum_proof: A file outside the intended directory retrieved with content shown; exact parameter and encoding that worked.
na_patterns: Reading a file inside the served directory (by design)
403/404/500 on ../ with no file returned
Filename reflected in error without content
Payload visibly blocked/normalized
overclaim_traps: Arbitrary file read equals RCE without a demonstrated execution path.
Inferring any file from one /etc/passwd.

label: Open redirect
description: Redirect to an attacker-controlled domain on a security-relevant path.
falsifier_hint: Redirect only on non-security-sensitive paths, or requires manual victim paste, or same-origin.
minimum_proof: Single URL redirecting to a hunter-controlled domain on auth callback/OAuth redirect_uri/password reset/login flow, plus a chain showing real impact.
na_patterns: Open redirect on non-sensitive paths with no chain
Redirect requiring manual paste
Same-origin redirects
overclaim_traps: Claiming token/code theft via redirect_uri that cannot be PoC'd; report only the proven redirect (typically Low).

label: Broken access control / IDOR / BOLA / auth bypass
description: Accessing resources or actions without the required authorization, including IDOR and auth bypass.
falsifier_hint: Endpoint returns data available unauthenticated by design, or only a protected route rendering an app shell without protected data.
minimum_proof: Specific endpoint/flow accessed without required auth state, sensitive target, bypass mechanism shown; for IDOR two hunter-controlled accounts A/B with A reading B's resource.
na_patterns: Sequential IDs without showing actual access
Reading own data via someone else's ID
Public-by-design resources
Admin endpoints only for admins (not broken)
Protected route that only renders client-side app shell
overclaim_traps: Mass account takeover without the takeover primitive on B.
Single-account discovery with cross-tenant impact but no second tenant.
Non-guessable identifier (UUIDv4) scored as enumerable (use AC:H).
Rating by mechanism not action for CSRF.

label: CSRF
description: Forcing an authenticated victim to perform a sensitive state change cross-site.
falsifier_hint: SameSite cookie blocks the request, or the action is low-impact (logout/search).
minimum_proof: Working PoC HTML page performing a sensitive action despite SameSite status, with SameSite verified.
na_patterns: CSRF on logout/search/low-impact actions
No token present without exploitation
SameSite Lax/Strict blocking the request
overclaim_traps: Account takeover via CSRF without a takeover chain.
Rating by mechanism rather than action value (cart add = Low).

label: SSRF
description: Server-side request forgery to internal or attacker-controlled endpoints.
falsifier_hint: Only DNS resolution, or outbound to public domains only, or request blocked by WAF/library/policy.
minimum_proof: Inbound request observed on hunter-controlled endpoint with reach demonstrated (internal host, metadata, localhost, protocol smuggling).
na_patterns: DNS resolution only
Blind SSRF to attacker domain only with no reach
SSRF to public domains only
Request blocked by WAF/library/network policy
overclaim_traps: Cloud metadata access without showing the metadata body.
Internal network scan without one successful internal hit.
Blind SSRF scored High/Critical without demonstrated reach (typically Low/N/A).

label: Server-side template injection
description: Untrusted input evaluated as a template on the server.
falsifier_hint: Literal reflection of template syntax with no evaluation, or math eval in a sandboxed engine without escape.
minimum_proof: Template syntax confirmed ({{7*7}} -> 49), engine identified, sandbox escape shown if sandboxed.
na_patterns: HTML/text reflection of {{7*7}} as literal
Math eval in sandboxed expression engine without escape path
Client-side template eval (CSTI) misreported as SSTI
overclaim_traps: Client-side template eval (Angular/Vue) reported as server RCE; it is XSS.

label: XXE
description: External entity resolution in an XML parser enabling file read or OOB callbacks.
falsifier_hint: Parser accepts DTD references but does not resolve entities, or only an error mentioning entity processing.
minimum_proof: External entity defined and resolved; file read content shown, or OOB callback with file content.
na_patterns: Parser accepts external DTD but does not resolve entities
Error mentioning entity processing without controlled file read
overclaim_traps: Using an entity-expansion bomb (billion laughs) as proof — that is DoS, not XXE.

label: Race condition
description: Broken invariant under concurrency producing an impossible state.
falsifier_hint: Multiple successes without a broken invariant, or idempotent endpoint duplicates.
minimum_proof: Broken invariant under concurrency with method and before/after persisted state shown (final ledger/balance), not just response codes.
na_patterns: 100 fast requests with several successes but no broken invariant
Duplicate submissions on idempotent endpoints
Response-time jitter mistaken for a race
Rate-limit bypass with no state impact
overclaim_traps: Double-spend claim from two 200s without persisted state change.
One lucky duplicate reported as reliable exploitation.
Scaling burst to thousands as proof (abuse, not evidence).

label: CORS misconfiguration
description: Reflected origin with credentials allowing cross-origin read of sensitive data.
falsifier_hint: Wildcard without credentials, fixed trusted origin, or endpoint returns only public data.
minimum_proof: ACAO reflects attacker origin AND ACAC true, endpoint returns session-authenticated sensitive data, working PoC page reads victim data cross-origin.
na_patterns: ACAO: * without ACAC: true
Reflected origin but only public/unauthenticated data
ACAC true with fixed trusted ACAO
Preflight reflects origin but real response does not
null origin without PoC
Bearer-token (header) auth, not cookies
overclaim_traps: Account takeover via CORS without a PoC page reading victim data.
High severity off header reflection alone.

label: Reentrancy
description: External call before state update allowing re-entry and double-spend.
falsifier_hint: Checks-effects-interactions respected, or reentrancy guard present and effective.
minimum_proof: Trace showing external call preceding state mutation and a reproducible re-entry path.
na_patterns: View-only external call with no state mutation after
Guard present and effective
overclaim_traps: Claiming reentrancy without a reproducible re-entry path.

label: Oracle manipulation
description: Price/valuation oracle can be moved within a single transaction (flash loan, stale feed).
falsifier_hint: Oracle uses TWAP/chainlink with sufficient staleness checks and no single-tx manipulation.
minimum_proof: Demonstrated price movement within one transaction affecting protocol state.
na_patterns: Oracle read-only with no state effect
Staleness checks effective
overclaim_traps: Claiming oracle manipulation without a demonstrated state effect.

label: Access control (web3)
description: Missing or bypassable authorization on privileged contract functions.
falsifier_hint: Function is intentionally public or properly guarded by role checks.
minimum_proof: Privileged action executed by an unauthorized account with tx evidence.
na_patterns: Public-by-design functions
Role checks effective
overclaim_traps: Claiming admin takeover without executing the privileged action.

label: Signature / permit replay
description: Signed message/permit reusable across contexts (missing nonce/domain separator).
falsifier_hint: Nonce incremented and domain separator present and validated.
minimum_proof: Same signature accepted twice or in a different context.
na_patterns: Nonce correctly incremented
Domain separator validated
overclaim_traps: Claiming replay without actually replaying.

label: Network exposure / misconfiguration
description: Exposed services, default credentials, or misconfigured network controls.
falsifier_hint: Service is intended to be public or properly firewalled.
minimum_proof: Reachable service with evidence of unintended exposure.
na_patterns: Intentionally public service
Properly firewalled
overclaim_traps: Claiming compromise without demonstrating access.

label: Unverified assumption is the attack surface
description: A developer belief treated as an invariant without ever being tested (balanceOf returns the real balance, this contract is trusted, the caller is always the owner). The untested belief is the entry point.
falsifier_hint: The assumption is enforced on-chain at every reachable path, or the belief is documented as intentionally out of scope.
minimum_proof: A reachable code path where the assumption does not hold, with the resulting state divergence shown.
na_patterns: Assumption enforced by an explicit require on every path
Belief is about off-chain data the contract never reads
overclaim_traps: Listing an assumption without showing a path that violates it.
Calling a documented design decision a vulnerability.

label: Token is a program, never a number
description: Any external token contract controls its own balanceOf, transfer, decimals, and fees. A malicious or non-standard token lies; accounting by returned value rather than by balance delta accounts by fiction.
falsifier_hint: The contract only interacts with a fixed, verified token set, or measures value by balance delta before and after the call.
minimum_proof: A token interaction whose accounting diverges from the actual balance delta, demonstrated with a lying token on a fork.
na_patterns: Fee-on-transfer token explicitly rejected by an allowlist
Value measured by balance delta, not by return value
overclaim_traps: Claiming a fee-on-transfer bug without showing the accounting break.
Assuming every ERC-20 behaves like the reference implementation.

label: Arithmetic is where trust goes to die
description: Precision loss, rounding direction, balanceAfter minus balanceBefore deltas, unchecked casts, and division before multiplication are the default fund-theft primitive.
falsifier_hint: All arithmetic is checked or uses a vetted fixed-point library, and rounding direction is proven to favour the protocol.
minimum_proof: A concrete input set where the computed result differs from the intended value in the attacker's favour, with the delta shown.
na_patterns: Solidity >=0.8 with no unchecked block on the path
Values are integers with no division on the path
overclaim_traps: Reporting a rounding direction without showing who gains.
Claiming overflow on a 0.8+ build without an unchecked block.

label: Storage layout is a writable interface
description: Packed slots, proxy storage collisions, uninitialized implementation slots, and EIP-1967 decoding (slot 0 is owner<<8|0x01, not a clean address) mean state layout is attacker-reachable.
falsifier_hint: Storage layout is collision-checked against the proxy pattern in use, and every implementation slot is initialized.
minimum_proof: A demonstrated slot collision or uninitialized slot that lets an attacker write privileged state.
na_patterns: Non-proxy contract with no delegatecall
Layout verified with a storage-diff tool against the ancestor
overclaim_traps: Reporting a packed slot as a collision without showing the overwrite.
Reading slot 0 as an address without EIP-1967 decoding.

label: Access control is a path, not a modifier
description: A modifier guards one function; the law asks which path reaches the effect without passing it — initializers, fallbacks, delegatecalls, role-bearing proxies, dual-guard revert frames.
falsifier_hint: Every path to the privileged effect passes an effective guard, including initializers and fallbacks.
minimum_proof: A call path that reaches the privileged effect without any guard, shown on a fork.
na_patterns: Single-guard function with no delegatecall or fallback route
Initializer is protected by an initializer modifier
overclaim_traps: Reporting a missing modifier on a function that is unreachable.
Claiming privilege escalation without executing the path.

label: Signatures are data, not authority
description: Replay, malleability, missing chainId or nonce binding, domain-separator confusion, and signer-versus-sender mismatch turn a valid signature into a skeleton key.
falsifier_hint: The signature is bound to chainId, contract address, nonce, and deadline, and the signer is recovered and checked.
minimum_proof: A signature accepted twice, or accepted from a different signer or chain than intended, demonstrated on a fork.
na_patterns: EIP-712 domain separator includes chainId and verifyingContract
Nonce is consumed before the effect is applied
overclaim_traps: Claiming replay without a second successful execution.
Reporting malleability on a path that never uses ecrecover.

label: Oracles are the cheapest object on the chain to move
description: Spot prices, single-source feeds, and reserve-derived prices bend under liquidity the attacker does not own. Price the protocol with a price you control.
falsifier_hint: Price comes from a manipulation-resistant source (TWAP, multi-oracle median) with a bounded deviation check.
minimum_proof: A price move the attacker can cause within one transaction, and the resulting protocol mispricing, shown on a fork.
na_patterns: Chainlink-style feed with staleness and bounds checks
Price only read for display, never for value transfer
overclaim_traps: Reporting spot-price use without showing the manipulable depth.
Claiming oracle attack on a read-only price display.

label: Ordering is permission
description: Public mempools and visible queues mean transaction order is an exploitable resource: frontrun, backrun, censorship. Anything valuable and visible is takeable by whoever pays to be first.
falsifier_hint: The operation is order-independent, or protected by a commit scheme, private mempool, or slippage bound.
minimum_proof: A profitable reordering demonstrated on a fork, or a mempool observation showing the sandwich window.
na_patterns: Commit-reveal or batch auction with uniform clearing price
Operation is idempotent and order-independent
overclaim_traps: Reporting frontrun risk on a permissioned/private mempool.
Claiming MEV without showing the extractable value.

label: Upgradability converts trust into a pending transaction
description: Every proxy is a future contract you have not met. Verify the implementation slot yourself, never trust the explorer's claim, and treat admin-key custody as the crown-jewel question.
falsifier_hint: Implementation slot verified on-chain, upgrade path is timelocked and multisigned, and admin keys are demonstrably controlled.
minimum_proof: The live implementation slot read from chain, compared against the explorer claim, with the admin address and its powers listed.
na_patterns: Immutable contract with no proxy or upgrade path
Upgrade requires a timelock the report accounts for
overclaim_traps: Trusting the explorer's verified-source label as the live code.
Reporting upgradeability as a bug when it is the stated design.

label: The chain boundary is a trust boundary
description: Cross-contract calls, bridge messaging, L1 to L2 relays, and cross-chain deployments each carry the source domain's assumptions into a domain that does not honour them. The handoff point is where the chain gadgets.
falsifier_hint: Every message is validated for source domain, and no source assumption is relied upon in the destination.
minimum_proof: A message accepted in the destination that the source domain would never have produced, demonstrated on a fork.
na_patterns: Single-chain contract with no external message entry point
Source domain is verified on every inbound message
overclaim_traps: Reporting cross-chain risk without showing the accepted forgery.
Assuming a bridge's verification covers the application layer.

label: Defaults are secrets
description: Hardcoded sponsor, committer, or prover keys, genesis byte-array keys, and real-format private keys committed as test fixtures are live credentials with a public address. Derive the address, check nonce and balance.
falsifier_hint: No key material in the repo or config, or every key is provably a well-known throwaway with zero balance and zero nonce.
minimum_proof: The key material located, its address derived, and the on-chain nonce and balance read to show whether it is live.
na_patterns: Well-known test key (e.g. anvil default) with zero balance
Key present but the account has never been funded
overclaim_traps: Reporting a hardcoded key without checking whether it holds value.
Claiming key control without deriving the address.

label: Deterministic derivation means leaked once, drained forever
description: BIP39 and fixed-curve derivations are time-invariant: a mnemonic committed today unlocks the same account on every future day and every chain it funded.
falsifier_hint: No mnemonic or seed in the repo, or the seed is provably unused across every chain it could have funded.
minimum_proof: The seed located and at least one derived address shown to hold or have held value.
na_patterns: Seed is a well-known test vector with no funded accounts
Derivation path is not used by any deployed contract
overclaim_traps: Reporting a test mnemonic as a live leak without checking balances.
Assuming one chain's emptiness proves all chains are empty.

label: Infrastructure endpoints are contract surface
description: RPC nodes are contracts with a JSON-RPC ABI: exposed debug, admin, and personal namespaces, CORS wildcard echoes, and unlocked accounts extend the EVM attack surface past the bytecode.
falsifier_hint: Dangerous namespaces are disabled or authenticated, CORS is not wildcard, and no account is unlocked.
minimum_proof: A dangerous namespace answering without authentication, or a CORS echo, captured as a request/response exchange.
na_patterns: Node is a public read-only endpoint by design
Namespace requires a bearer token that is not held
overclaim_traps: Reporting an open RPC as a vulnerability when it is a public endpoint.
Claiming admin access from a 405 or 401 response.

label: The fork is a fossil record
description: A lending fork inherits every ancestor vulnerability plus every divergence bug introduced by the port. Diff against the ancestor before trusting any upstream audit claim.
falsifier_hint: The fork is diffed against its ancestor and every inherited fix is confirmed present.
minimum_proof: A diff against the ancestor showing an inherited vulnerability still reachable, or a port-introduced divergence.
na_patterns: Original codebase, not a fork
Ancestor fix confirmed present in the fork
overclaim_traps: Reporting an ancestor bug the fork already fixed.
Trusting an upstream audit without diffing the fork.

label: Liquidity is an attack multiplier
description: Flash loans make any price the price and any governance threshold a day-pass: evaluate every economic check as if the attacker can rent majority power for one block.
falsifier_hint: The check is not movable within one transaction, or the flash-loaned capital cannot satisfy it.
minimum_proof: A single-transaction path using borrowed capital to satisfy the check, demonstrated on a fork.
na_patterns: Check requires capital locked across blocks
Governance uses snapshot voting that predates the loan
overclaim_traps: Reporting flash-loan risk on a time-locked or snapshotted check.
Claiming governance capture without the borrowed-vote math.

label: Time and finality assumptions fail under stress
description: Block timestamps, reorg windows, bridge lag, and sequencer downtime are consensus-level inputs that contracts read as facts. Attack the lag, not the lock.
falsifier_hint: The contract tolerates reorgs, sequencer downtime, and bridge lag within its stated bounds.
minimum_proof: A state that becomes invalid under a realistic reorg, delay, or downtime window.
na_patterns: Timestamp used only for coarse ordering with a wide margin
Finality is waited on explicitly before the effect
overclaim_traps: Reporting timestamp dependence on a check with a wide tolerance.
Assuming L1 finality guarantees an L2 state.

label: Replay is the default, uniqueness is the exception
description: Any message, permit, or calldata not bound to a chain, contract, nonce, and deadline can be rebroadcast where it still works. Assume replay until proven unique.
falsifier_hint: Every accepted message is bound to chainId, verifyingContract, nonce, and deadline, and the nonce is consumed atomically.
minimum_proof: A message executed twice, or executed on a chain or contract it was not intended for.
na_patterns: EIP-712 domain separator with all four bindings
Nonce invalidated before the effect is applied
overclaim_traps: Claiming replay on a nonce-protected path.
Reporting cross-chain replay without a second successful execution.

label: A verifier you cannot run is a claim you cannot trust
description: External audit claims, explorer labels, and docs are hypotheses. Verify against source and live state — evidence or nothing.
falsifier_hint: The claim has been re-derived from source and confirmed against live chain state.
minimum_proof: The independent verification run, with its output, beside the claim it tests.
na_patterns: Claim re-verified from source and live state in this audit
Claim is about a contract not in scope
overclaim_traps: Repeating an audit finding without re-deriving it.
Treating a verified explorer label as the live bytecode.

label: Unproven impact is not impact
description: A vulnerability that cannot be demonstrated stays theoretical. proven-in-code needs a mainnet address and chainId; proven-live needs a tx hash or state proof. A theoretical finding never masquerades as a critical.
falsifier_hint: The impact has been demonstrated at the claimed proof level, or the finding is explicitly labelled theoretical.
minimum_proof: The proof artefact matching the claimed level: address plus chainId for proven-in-code, tx hash or state proof for proven-live.
na_patterns: Finding explicitly labelled theoretical with no impact claim
Proof artefact present and matches the claimed level
overclaim_traps: Labelling a finding proven without the matching artefact.
Fabricating a mainnet tx hash — the one unforgivable violation.
